samples.summary: Preview-fit tests only bound the pattern from above; an over-shrunken (invisible) pattern still passes
samples.evidence: Both new assertions on the scaled pattern are one-sided: `expect(dash + gap).toBeLessThanOrEqual(32)` (lines 73 and 89) plus a ratio check `dash/gap ≈ refDash/refGap`. `fitPattern` (stroke-preview.tsx:26-31) is supposed to scale the cycle to exactly `PREVIEW_W / 2 = 32`, but nothing asserts that. A regression that scaled to, say, `[0.12, 0.08]` (or any tiny factor) keeps the ratio, satisfies `gap > 0` and `sum <= 32`, and would render as a near-solid grey line — exactly the user-visible defect these tests exist to prevent. An `expect(dash + gap).toBeCloseTo(32)` (or a lower bound) would close it. The dotted test (line 64-73) additionally never asserts `gap > 0`, unlike the dashed one at line 90.

samples.summary: The weight menu's StrokePreview rows are only tested at 4px, so the new pattern-fitting on the 16px row is uncovered there
samples.evidence: `border-picker.tsx:175` renders `StrokePreview` for each weight row including 16px, which now goes through `fitPattern`. The only weight-menu dash assertion, 'carries the current dash into the weight previews' (border-picker.test.tsx:153-165), checks the 4px row with an exact `dashArray('dotted', 4).join(' ')` equality — a cycle of 16, below the 32 threshold, so it exercises only the untouched branch. If `fitPattern` broke for the large-weight rows the weight menu would show 16px Dashed as a solid bar and no test in this file would fail (the dash-menu tests cover the other call site at line 208).

samples.summary: fitPattern's threshold boundary (cycle exactly 32 / just over) has no test
samples.evidence: `if (cycle <= max) return pattern;` is only exercised well below the boundary (width 1, cycle 10/4; width 4, cycle 16) and well above (width 16, cycle 160/64). The off-by-one edge — e.g. dashed at width 3 (`[18,12]`, cycle 30, untouched) versus width 4 (`[24,16]`, cycle 40, scaled) — is not pinned by any assertion, so flipping `<=` to `<` or changing `PREVIEW_W / 2` would not be detected.
